title: Troubleshooting playbook
summary: Map the real error messages from curl, browsers, .NET, Java and Go to a cause, a command that confirms it, and the fix.

steps.title: The playbook
body: | Error you see | Usual cause | Confirm with | Fix |

| `curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate` | server doesn't send the intermediate, or private root not trusted | `openssl s_client -connect h:443 -servername h -showcerts` (count the certs) | serve `fullchain.pem`; or install the root |
| `curl: (60) ... self-signed certificate in certificate chain` | the root is not trusted by this client | same, look at the last `i:` | install the root / `--cacert` |
| `NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` | host not in the SAN | `openssl x509 -noout -ext subjectAltName` | reissue with the right SAN |
| `NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID`, `certificate has expired` | expired (or the client's clock is wrong) | `openssl x509 -noout -dates`; `date` | renew; fix the clock |

| `AuthenticationException: The remote certificate is invalid because of errors in the certificate chain: PartialChain` (.NET, `RemoteCertificateChainErrors`) | missing intermediate | `s_client -showcerts` | serve the full chain |
| ... `RemoteCertificateNameMismatch` | wrong host name | `-ext subjectAltName` | SAN |

| `PKIX path building failed: unable to find valid certification path to requested target` (Java) | root not in `cacerts`, or missing intermediate | `keytool -list -cacerts`; `s_client` | `keytool -importcert -cacerts`; full chain |
| `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` (Go) | root not in the container's store | `ls /etc/ssl/certs` in the container | add `ca-certificates` + your root to the image |

Two habits: **reproduce with the same client** (curl and Chrome disagree because Chrome fetches missing intermediates), and **always pass the real host name** (`-servername`), or you diagnose the default certificate.

steps.prompt: Match each error to its most likely cause.
pairs: the server sends only its leaf
the host is not in the SAN
the Go program's store doesn't have the root

steps.prompt: `curl https://api.shop.example` fails with `curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. Chrome opens the site with a padlock. The site uses a well-known public CA. Most likely?
options: The server sends only the leaf; Chrome fills the gap from its cache or AIA, curl does not
curl's CA bundle is out of date
steps.explain: A public root is in every store, so the gap is the intermediate. Confirm with `s_client -showcerts`: you will see only `0 s:`.

steps.prompt: You run `openssl s_client -connect api.shop.example:443 -servername api.shop.example -showcerts </dev/null`. How many certificates did the server send? (Then you know what to fix.)
code: verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify error:num=21:unable to verify the first certificate
i:C = US, O = Example Trust, CN = Example TLS Issuing CA 2
Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)
steps.explain: Only depth 0: the leaf. Fix it on the server by serving `cat cert.pem intermediate.pem > fullchain.pem` (nginx `ssl_certificate fullchain.pem;`).

steps.prompt: Work a `NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` ticket for `portal.shop.example` from report to fix.
lines: `openssl s_client -connect portal.shop.example:443 -servername portal.shop.example </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -ext subjectAltName`
Deploy it and reload the web server
Run the curl command again and check `subject` and `SSL certificate verify ok`
steps.explain: Reproduce, confirm the SAN, fix, deploy, re-test. Skipping the confirm step is how you reissue a certificate that was fine while the DNS pointed at the wrong server.

items: Java truststore lacks the corporate root
wrong EKU (clientAuth on a web server)

steps.title: Chain status flags and openssl error numbers
body: .NET reports chain problems as `X509ChainStatusFlags`; openssl as numbered errors. Same problems, different names:
| `X509ChainStatusFlags` | openssl verify error | Meaning |
| `PartialChain` | 20 `unable to get local issuer certificate` | an issuer could not be found |
| `UntrustedRoot` | 19 `self-signed certificate in certificate chain` | the path ends at a root nobody trusts |
| `NotTimeValid` | 10 `certificate has expired` / 9 `not yet valid` | outside notBefore/notAfter |
| `NotValidForUsage` | 26 `unsupported certificate purpose` | EKU doesn't allow serverAuth |
| `Revoked` | 23 `certificate revoked` | on a CRL / OCSP says revoked |
In your own .NET code, print them instead of guessing:
```csharp
handler.ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback = (msg, cert, chain, errors) =>
if (errors != SslPolicyErrors.None)
Console.Error.WriteLine($"{errors}: {string.Join(", ", chain!.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status))}");
return errors == SslPolicyErrors.None;     // log, but still refuse

code: var root = DojoCert("CN=Shop Root CA", null, true, naYear: 2040);
var inter = DojoCert("CN=Shop Issuing CA", root, true);
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: The leaf's EKU is clientAuth (`...3.2`) but the chain is checked for serverAuth (`...3.1`): `NotValidForUsage`, openssl's "unsupported certificate purpose".

steps.prompt: A Go service in an `alpine` container fails with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` calling `https://intranet.corp.example`. The same binary works on your laptop. Best fix?
options: Add `ca-certificates` and the corporate root to the image and run `update-ca-certificates` in the Dockerfile
Install the root on the Docker host
Rebuild the binary with a newer Go
steps.explain: The container has its own filesystem and its own (here: missing) trust store. The host's store doesn't apply inside it.

steps.title: Translate .NET chain errors to openssl
prompt: Write `string OpensslError(X509ChainStatusFlags flag)` that returns the openssl verify message for a .NET chain status flag, so a log line from a .NET service can be searched next to openssl output:
| `PartialChain` | `20 unable to get local issuer certificate` |
| anything else | `? ` + the flag's name (for example `? NotSignatureValid`) |
The tests also break real chains and feed your function the flags `X509Chain` reports.
solution: X509ChainStatusFlags.PartialChain => "20 unable to get local issuer certificate",
X509ChainStatusFlags.UntrustedRoot => "19 self-signed certificate in certificate chain",
hints: A `switch` expression on `flag` is the neatest form.

var dojoInt = DojoCert("CN=Shop Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
string DojoRun(X509Certificate2 leaf, bool trust, bool sendInt, int year = 2030)
Dojo.Eq("missing intermediate", "20 unable to get local issuer certificate", DojoRun(dojoGood, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("untrusted root", "19 self-signed certificate in certificate chain", DojoRun(dojoGood, false, true));
Dojo.Eq("expired (checked in 2032)", "10 certificate has expired", DojoRun(dojoGood, true, true, 2032));
Dojo.Eq("wrong EKU", "26 unsupported certificate purpose", DojoRun(DojoCert("CN=c.example", dojoInt, false, "c.example", "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2", 2030, 2031), true, true));
